title: Member-Request Ceiling Where the Member Has Prior Quantity Limit Authorizations or Cases
content:
For a member-filed first-time quantity limit exception request under the Utilization Management Program, the member-request ceiling is the drug's limit times a share of the package's maximum exception multiple, and the member's quantity limit history for the drug over the last 24 months sets that share:

| Member's history for the drug in the last 24 months | Ceiling |
|---|---|
| A quantity limit authorization for the drug that took effect within the last 24 months | the drug's limit times the whole of the package's maximum exception multiple |
| No such authorization, but a quantity limit exception case for the drug opened within the last 24 months | the drug's limit times seven eighths (0.875) of the package's maximum exception multiple |
| Neither | no change to the ceiling under this rule |

An authorization counts by its effective date and a case by the date it was opened. The 24 months end on the filing date: a record counts when it is dated after the same day of the month 24 months before the filing date. Any quantity limit authorization for the drug counts, whatever brought it about.

## The ceiling in figures (hypothetical history; package multiples as the review packages state them)

| Package's maximum exception multiple | Whole multiple | Seven eighths of it | Ubrelvy (limit 16), whole multiple | Ubrelvy, seven eighths |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.0 (Northbridge Clinical Essentials, Standard, Advanced) | 2.0 | 1.75 | 32 | 28 |
| 1.5 (Northbridge Clinical Advanced Plus, Comprehensive, Comprehensive Specialty) | 1.5 | 1.3125 | 24 | 21 |

### Points of judgement

- A member who held a quantity limit authorization for the drug that took effect 20 months before filing, and also had a case opened 10 months before, takes the whole multiple: the authorization decides.
- A case opened 25 months before filing falls outside the window and does not count.
